calibration_scale_interpretation.plausibility_statement: The required correction is small relative to the already observed uncalibrated contact-convention sensitivity, so it is plausibly a calibration/definition margin. It is not an accepted noise-budget claim because no measured TCP, contact patch, plane normal, or force-frame calibration has been recorded.
calibration_scale_interpretation.model_change_statement: Any accepted recovery must update the measured geometry/normal/gate definition or produce a calibrated model; the legacy sphere-center convention is only a sensitivity comparison and is not an acceptable model change by itself.

accepted diagnostic orientation definition that states whether force-normal-only or full frame rotation is the gate

v85_objective_answers.question: 1. What exact orientation margin remains at the hardest currently known row?
v85_objective_answers.answer: 0.0005664520369604714 rad (0.03245531101442353 deg) over the 0.119 rad gate at time0p01_gate0p119:weighted_kp0_normal1.

v85_objective_answers.question: 2. How large a contact normal angular correction would close that margin?
v85_objective_answers.answer: At least 0.0005664520369604714 rad (0.03245531101442353 deg), assuming the correction acts in the error-reducing direction.

v85_objective_answers.question: 3. What equivalent contact-point/TCP/base-z correction is implied?
v85_objective_answers.answer: 0.014963398168061883 mm (14.963398168061882 um) using the v84 high-end terminal slope proxy of 0.03785584200850284 rad/mm.

v85_objective_answers.question: 4. Which correction sizes are plausibly below measurement/calibration noise?
v85_objective_answers.answer: The 0.0325 deg normal correction and 15 um equivalent geometry correction are small relative to the current unmeasured model-convention ambiguity, but no accepted measurement noise budget exists yet.

v85_objective_answers.question: 5. Which physical measurements are required before a hardware claim?
v85_objective_answers.answer: measured mounted-stack TCP/contact point from robot flange or design flange datum; verified contact sphere/patch convention and whether the 85 mm EOAT datum is center or surface; plane/contact normal measured in the robot base frame; force sensor zero, frame, compensation, and UR RTDE versus OnRobot source reconciliation; accepted diagnostic orientation definition that states whether force-normal-only or full frame rotation is the gate

v85_objective_answers.question: 6. Do existing metrics justify accepting 0.119, 0.11955, 0.1196, or 0.11995 rad?
v85_objective_answers.answer: They show which rows recover at those gates, but they do not justify a replacement diagnostic gate without calibrated geometry/normal evidence.

v85_objective_answers.question: 7. Does this support more Stage B qdot tuning?
v85_objective_answers.answer: No. The hardest weighted rows report 0.0 qdot saturation and miss only by a small orientation margin.
